name: Commercial property and casualty new business underwriting
summary: This process takes one new business submission for a small or mid-size commercial property and casualty account from a broker through clearance, triage, data gathering, risk assessment, pricing, referral, quote, negotiation, bind and policy issuance. Underwriting assistants log and re-key emailed ACORD forms and order third-party data, underwriters assess and price the risk within their authority, senior underwriters approve referrals, and policy services build and check the policy after binding. Most submissions are declined or lost to other carriers, so much underwriting effort produces no policy; elapsed time goes to underwriter queues, waits for missing broker information and the broker's market comparison, and the post-bind issuance backlog.

baseline.org_archetype: A US regional property and casualty insurer with about 2,500 employees writing small and middle market commercial package, general liability, property, auto and umbrella business through independent agents and brokers.
baseline.notes: Excludes micro small business policies quoted straight-through on agency portals and excludes renewals; the same underwriters also handle renewals.

unit_of_work: one new business submission (one commercial account, one or more lines)
trigger: A broker submits a new commercial account to the carrier for a quote.
end_state: A policy is issued, or the submission is declined, withdrawn, or quoted but not taken.

volume.seasonality: Peaks before 1 January and 1 July effective dates; firming market conditions in 2020-2022 raised submission counts as brokers shopped accounts more widely.

evidence.note: Author estimate for a regional carrier of about 2,500 employees.

produces.to: Risk control (post-bind surveys) and reinsurance accumulation reporting

systems.name: Policy administration system (clearance, rating, issuance, billing)
Rating worksheets and pricing model (spreadsheet for mid-market risks)
Third-party data: business credit, property characteristics, catastrophe model, motor vehicle records
Quote, binder and policy document generation

steps.name: Broker sends new business submission
steps.description: A retail broker emails the submission to the carrier's submissions mailbox or underwriter: ACORD commercial application and line sections, schedule of locations and values, vehicle and driver lists, five years of loss runs, prior policy, target premium and the effective date, usually 30 to 90 days ahead.

error.defect_description: None introduced (gaps are found later).

evidence.note: Underwriters receive applications through agents and brokers (BLS); package contents reflect standard ACORD practice, an author description. Broker effort is not carrier labour, so touch is 0.

steps.name: Log submission and key application data
steps.description: An underwriting assistant opens the email, saves the attachments, creates a submission record in the workbench and re-types the insured's name, address, FEIN, industry class codes, lines requested, effective date and broker from the ACORD forms.

error.defect_description: Name, class code or effective date keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Clerk duties from BLS; re-keying from emailed PDFs was common in 2019-2022; minutes and mailbox backlog are author estimates.

steps.name: Run clearance, licence and sanctions checks
steps.description: The assistant searches the policy system for the same insured under another broker, existing policies and prior declines, confirms the broker is licensed and appointed in the state, and screens the insured against the OFAC list. An account already cleared for another broker is blocked.

error.defect_description: Duplicate submission not found, causing a broker conflict later.

control.basis: Producer licensing (NAIC Model 218: no business from or commission to unlicensed producers) and OFAC sanctions regulations

next.condition: blocked by another broker's clearance, licence problem or sanctions hit

evidence.note: Licensing and sanctions duties from the cited rules; clearance by insured is standard practice; the 10% block rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Triage submission against appetite
steps.description: An underwriter reads the submission summary, checks class of business, size, locations, catastrophe exposure and loss history against the appetite guide, and decides whether to pursue it and how urgently, given the effective date and broker relationship.

error.defect_description: Good risk declined or an out-of-appetite risk pursued.

evidence.note: Screening applicants against established criteria is a core underwriter task (BLS); the 30% triage decline rate, minutes and queue are author estimates.

steps.name: Send declination or block notice
steps.description: The assistant emails the broker that the carrier is declining the submission, or that the account is blocked because another broker has it, records the reason code and closes the submission.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check completeness and order third-party data
steps.description: The assistant compares the package with the checklist for the lines requested, and orders business credit, property characteristics and catastrophe model results for property locations, and motor vehicle records for fleet drivers. Missing loss runs, unsigned applications or incomplete location schedules are listed.

error.defect_description: A missing item is not flagged until the underwriter reviews.

evidence.note: Third-party data ordering was common for mid-market risks; the 55% incomplete rate and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Request missing information from broker
steps.description: The assistant or underwriter emails the broker a list of what is still needed (current loss runs, building updates, driver lists, supplemental questionnaires) and diaries a follow-up.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Wait for broker and insured to supply information
steps.description: The broker asks the insured and prior carriers for the missing items; loss runs from prior carriers and supplemental applications often take days. Some brokers place the account elsewhere instead.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Assess the risk
steps.description: The underwriter reviews the operations, exposures, building construction and protection, catastrophe model output, loss runs (frequency, severity, loss ratio, open claims), financial strength and driver records, and decides whether to quote, order a loss control survey first, or decline.

error.defect_description: Exposure misunderstood or adverse loss trend missed.

next.condition: loss control survey needed before quoting

evidence.note: Risk assessment tasks from BLS; minutes, the submission queue and outcome shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Survey the premises (loss control)
steps.description: A loss control representative schedules a visit with the insured, inspects buildings, fire protection, housekeeping, fleet and safety programmes, and writes a survey report with recommendations and a risk grade for the underwriter.

error.defect_description: Hazard missed or report late for the quote deadline.

evidence.note: Pre-quote surveys are used for larger property and casualty risks; share, time on site and scheduling wait are author estimates.

steps.name: Key exposures into rating system
steps.description: The assistant enters locations, values, class codes, payroll or sales, vehicles and limits from the submission into the rating system or the mid-market rating spreadsheet, re-typing figures already captured in the workbench.

error.defect_description: Value, class or payroll keyed wrongly, mispricing the risk.

evidence.note: Re-keying between workbench and rater was common in 2019-2022; author estimate.

steps.name: Price and structure the quote
steps.description: The underwriter runs the rating with the filed base rates, applies schedule rating credits or debits and experience modification within the filed rating plan, compares with the technical price, and sets limits, deductibles, exclusions and endorsements; risks beyond the letter of authority go to referral.

error.defect_description: Credit beyond guidelines or wrong form attached.

control.basis: State property and casualty rating laws: premiums must follow the insurer's filed rates and rating plans

evidence.note: Rating software use is described by BLS; the filed-rate requirement is state law (no statute opened); minutes and referral share are author estimates.

steps.name: Approve referral
steps.description: A senior underwriter or underwriting manager reviews the referral memo for risks that exceed the underwriter's letter of authority (size, class, catastrophe accumulation, schedule credits beyond limit) and approves, approves with changed terms, or declines.

error.defect_description: Accumulation or adverse trend overlooked.

control.basis: Underwriting letters of authority and referral rules

evidence.note: Authority and referral practice is universal in commercial underwriting; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare and send quote
steps.description: The assistant generates the quote proposal with premium by line, terms, subjectivities and the terrorism coverage offer and premium disclosure, checks it against the underwriter's notes and emails it to the broker.

error.defect_description: Quote premium or terms differ from the underwriter's notes.

control.basis: Terrorism Risk Insurance Program disclosure, 31 CFR 50.10: terrorism premium and federal share disclosed at the time of offer

evidence.note: Disclosure timing stated in the rule; minutes and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Broker presents quote to the insured
steps.description: The broker compares the quote with other carriers' quotes and the incumbent's renewal, presents options to the insured and comes back to accept, ask for changes, or say the account went elsewhere.
outputs: bind request, counter-request or loss notice

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: asks for better price or terms
placed with another carrier or renewed with incumbent

evidence.note: Quote outcome shares (about 35-40% of quotes eventually bound) are author estimates; no hit-ratio source was opened.

steps.name: Negotiate terms with broker
steps.description: The underwriter reviews the broker's counter-request (lower premium, higher limits, removed exclusion), re-prices within authority or refers it, and replies with revised terms or holds firm.

error.defect_description: Concession beyond guidelines.

next.condition: cannot meet the target: account lost

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Receive bind order and check subjectivities
steps.description: The assistant logs the broker's bind request, checks that subjectivities are met (signed application, no-known-loss letter, inspection access, payment plan) and that the effective date and terms match the quote.

error.defect_description: Missing subjectivity not noticed.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Approve bind and issue binder
steps.description: The underwriter confirms nothing material has changed since the quote, approves the bind and issues the binder to the broker as temporary evidence of coverage until the policy is issued.

error.defect_description: Binder terms differ from the quote.

control.basis: Underwriting authority: only an authorised underwriter may bind coverage

evidence.note: Binder definition from IRMI; times and refusal share are author estimates.

steps.name: Enter policy in policy administration system
steps.description: A policy issuance specialist builds the policy in the policy administration system from the binder and rating worksheet, re-keying locations, vehicles, limits, premiums and endorsements and attaching the forms.

error.defect_description: Form, location or premium keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Issuance backlogs of days to weeks after binding were common; times and error rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Check issued policy against the bound terms
steps.description: A quality checker compares the declarations, forms, endorsements and premium with the binder and quote line by line and sends errors back to the issuance specialist.

error.defect_description: Error passes to the issued policy.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Issue policy documents and book premium
steps.description: The policy system finalises the policy, generates the documents and invoice, and the specialist sends the policy to the broker; the premium is booked for billing.

error.defect_description: Documents sent to the wrong broker contact.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Close quote not taken
steps.description: When the broker reports the account went elsewhere, or the effective date passes without a bind, the assistant records the lost reason (price, terms, incumbent retained) and the winning premium if known, and closes the submission.
inputs: broker response or lapsed effective date

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Clearance block
exceptions.description: Another broker has already cleared the account, the broker is not licensed or appointed, or the insured is a sanctions match.

exceptions.name: Incomplete submission
exceptions.description: Loss runs, location values, driver lists or supplemental applications are missing and the assistant must chase the broker.

exceptions.name: Loss control survey before quote
exceptions.description: The underwriter needs a site survey before pricing a larger or hazardous risk.

exceptions.name: Referral
exceptions.description: Size, class, catastrophe accumulation or credits exceed the underwriter's authority and a senior underwriter must approve.

exceptions.name: Negotiation
exceptions.description: The broker asks for a lower premium or broader terms and the underwriter re-prices.

exceptions.name: Issuance error
exceptions.description: The checker finds the issued policy does not match the bound terms.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from submission received to final outcome (issued, declined, withdrawn or not taken)
benchmarks.population: US small and mid-market commercial P&C new business submissions, 2019-2022

evidence.note: No source with measured submission cycle times was opened. Estimate: triage declines close within days; quotes take one to three weeks; quotes not taken close at or near the effective date; bound policies are issued two to six weeks after binding.

benchmarks.value: at time of offer and renewal
benchmarks.population: Commercial P&C policies subject to the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program

evidence.note: Stated in 31 CFR 50.10(b).
Stated in BLS OEWS.

pain_points.description: Submission data arrives as emailed PDFs and is re-typed into the workbench, the rater and again into the policy system, causing errors that the issuance checker must catch.

evidence.note: Author judgement of 2019-2022 practice.

pain_points.description: Underwriters spend much of their time on submissions that are declined or lost, while good submissions wait days in their queues and miss broker deadlines.

evidence.note: Follows from the modelled outcome shares: under a fifth of submissions become policies.

pain_points.description: Incomplete submissions cause chase loops for loss runs and location data.

evidence.note: Author judgement.

pain_points.description: Referrals wait for a small number of senior underwriters, and policies are issued weeks after binding, leaving brokers waiting for documents.

evidence.note: Author judgement.

sources.supports: Insurers must disclose the premium for terrorism losses covered by the Program and the federal share, as a separate line item at the time of offer and renewal

sources.title: Producer Licensing Model Act (Model 218)
sources.supports: Insurers may not pay commission to an unlicensed person; knowingly accepting business from an unlicensed individual is grounds for action; appointment notices

sources.title: Binder (insurance definition)
sources.supports: A binder is a legal agreement issued by an agent or insurer giving temporary evidence of insurance until the policy can be issued

sources.title: 31 CFR 501.603 Reports of blocked property
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Blocked property, including insurance contracts with sanctioned parties, must be reported to OFAC within 10 business days

assumptions: External steps (broker, insured) carry zero touch time; their effort is inside the waits, so the staffing comparison reflects carrier labour only.

Outcome shares (10% blocked, 30% of cleared submissions declined at triage, about 55% of submissions quoted, about 35-40% of quotes bound, about 18% of submissions issued) are author estimates; no published quote or hit-ratio source was opened.
The web search budget ran out before this workflow was researched, so sources are limited to pages whose addresses were already known; most step times and the cycle-time benchmark are tier C.
Rating against filed rates and plans is a legal requirement in most states for admitted business; it is recorded as fixed by law but no statute was opened.
Loss control surveys before quoting are modelled for 15% of assessed risks; many carriers survey after binding instead, which is outside this workflow.
Stated FTEs are about 15% above the hands-on time implied at 130 productive hours a month; underwriters' renewal and portfolio work is excluded.

Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 hourly wage x 1.49 (benefits: wages are 67% of compensation in financial activities, which includes insurance, BLS ECEC Dec 2021) x 1.2 for overhead (author estimate), about 1.8 x wage.
